### advectionDiffusion3d

The example `advectionDiffusion3d` acts as a mesh-convergence test for a numerical solution to the initial value problem

$$
\begin{cases}
\partial_{t} \chi (\mathbf{x}, t) + \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \mathbf{F} \left( \chi(\mathbf{x}, t) \right) - \mu \Delta_{\mathbf{x}} \chi (\mathbf{x}, t) = 0  \quad & \text{in }\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{I}, \\
\chi(\mathbf{x}, 0 ) \equiv \chi_{0} (\mathbf{x})  \quad & \text{in } \mathcal{X},
\end{cases}
$$

where $\chi : \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{I} \to \mathbb{R}$ is the conservative variable dependent on space $\mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ and time $t \in \mathcal{I} \subseteq \mathbb{R}_{0}^{+}$, $\mathbf{F} \equiv \mathbf{u} \chi$ is a linear function defined by the advection velocity $\mathbf{u} = \left(u_x, u_y, u_{z}\right)^{\mathrm{T}} \in \mathbb{R}^{3}$, and $\mu > 0$ denotes the diffusion coefficient.
Note that the domain $\mathcal{X} = [-1 , 1]^{3}$ is periodic.

The example implements a smooth initial profile $\chi_{0}^{\mathrm{s}} (\mathbf{x})$ and an unsmooth version $\chi_{0}^{\mathrm{u}} (\mathbf{x})$.
The former is a three-dimensional extrusion of the initial pulse in the `advectionDiffusion2d` example, such that the equation admits the analytical solution [@dapelo:21; @simonis:20; @simonis:23]

$$
\chi^{\star,\mathrm{s}}\left(x, y, z, t\right) = \sin \left[ \pi \left(x - u_x t\right) \right] \sin \left[ \pi \left( y - u_y t\right) \right] \sin \left[ \pi \left(z - u_z t\right) \right] \exp \left( - 3 \mu \pi^{2} t \right).
$$

The latter comprises a Dirac delta at $x_0$ as the initial pulse, which induces a Dirac comb as a super-positioned analytical solution [@dapelo:21]

$$
\chi^{\star,\mathrm{u}}\left(x,y,z,t\right) =  \frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi\mu t }} \sum\limits_{k\in \mathbb{Z}} \exp\left( \frac{-\left( x - x_0 - u_{x} t + 2 k\right)^{2}  }{4 \mu t }\right) + 1
$$

For each case, several error norms over the domain measure the deviations from the analytical solution.
For the default setting, the outputs of three subsequent simulation runs are stored in a subfolder structure in `./tmp` and directly post-processed for visualization.
Via issuing the command

```{.bash}
python3 advectionDiffusion3dPlot.py
```

an error plot is produced, which numerically validates the second order convergence for both initializations, under the constraints on the grid Péclet number derived in [@dapelo:21].
